title: Mission 07: The Log Watch
story: The night shift pages you: the service log is 500 lines and growing, and nobody has time to read all of it. Ends first - that is the log watcher's creed. head reads beginnings, tail reads endings, and together they can cut any slice you name.

badge.name: The Log Watch: Sliced
badge.desc: Mastered head and tail by slicing a live service log every way the night shift needs.

tasks.brief: Read BRIEFING7.txt in your department directory. The boot sequence lives at the top of logwatch/service.log: save its FIRST 10 lines (head's default) to logwatch/first10.txt.

checks.fail: first10.txt is not exactly the first 10 lines of service.log.

tasks.brief: What just happened? Save the LAST 10 lines of service.log (tail's default) to logwatch/last10.txt.

checks.fail: last10.txt is not exactly the last 10 lines of service.log.

tasks.brief: The boot audit wants more context: the first 25 lines, to logwatch/boot25.txt. Both commands take a line-count option.

checks.fail: boot25.txt is not exactly the first 25 lines of service.log.

tasks.brief: For the pager alert, just the final 3 lines: logwatch/alert3.txt.

checks.fail: alert3.txt is not exactly the last 3 lines of service.log.

tasks.brief: The incident started at exactly line 42. Extract THAT ONE LINE to logwatch/line42.txt - the classic move pipes one command's slice into the other.

checks.fail: line42.txt must contain exactly line 42 of service.log and nothing else (slice the head, then take its tail).

tasks.brief: The last 20 lines are shutdown noise. Produce logwatch/trimmed.txt: EVERYTHING EXCEPT the last 20 lines (head can count from the end with a minus).

checks.fail: trimmed.txt should be the whole log MINUS its final 20 lines (head accepts a negative count).

tasks.brief: The morning crew only needs the log FROM line 100 to the end: logwatch/from100.txt (tail can start AT a line number with a plus).

checks.fail: from100.txt must start at line 100 and run to the end (tail accepts +N to start at line N).
service.log itself was modified. A log watcher reads; the log is evidence.

tasks.brief: BONUS: the header magic is the first 32 BYTES (not lines) of service.log. Save exactly those to logwatch/magic.txt (one of the two commands slices bytes too).

checks.fail: magic.txt must be exactly the first 32 bytes of service.log (a byte-count option, not a line count).
